easy.def: A small animal with long ears that hops.
examples: The rabbit hopped across the grass.
I feed my pet rabbit a carrot.
The rabbit has soft fur.

more.def: A small furry animal with long ears and a short tail that moves by hopping.
examples: The rabbit dug a burrow under the old tree.
Rabbits nibble on clover and lettuce.
A wild rabbit froze when it saw the fox.

easy.def: A contest to see who is fastest.
examples: We ran a race.
I won the race.
The race was fun.

more.def: A contest to see who can go the fastest or reach a place first.
examples: She won the race by one second.
The horses lined up for the big race.
Our class held a relay race on field day.

easy.def: To try to go the fastest.
examples: We race to the tree.
The cars raced.
She races her brother.

more.def: To compete to see who can go fastest or arrive first.
examples: The boys raced each other to the gate.
Sailboats raced across the bay.
I raced my sister up the stairs.

easy.def: A machine that finds things by sending out waves.
examples: The radar showed the storm.
Planes use radar.
The radar found the plane.

more.def: A machine that uses radio waves to find where things are.
examples: The radar showed a storm coming.
Airplanes use radar to avoid hills.
The radar spotted the flock of birds.

easy.def: A machine that plays sounds sent through the air.
examples: Turn on the radio.
We listen to the radio in the car.
The radio plays music.

more.def: A device that receives sounds sent through the air, such as music and news.
examples: We listen to music on the radio in the car.
A weather report came over the radio.
Grandpa fixed the old radio.

easy.def: Water that falls from the sky.
examples: Rain fell on the roof.
I love the sound of rain.
We played inside in the rain.

more.def: Drops of water that fall from clouds.
examples: Heavy rain filled the creek.
Rain tapped on the window.
We walked home in the rain.

easy.def: To fall as drops of water from the sky.
examples: It rains a lot here.
It rained all day.
I hope it does not rain.

more.def: To fall from the clouds in drops.
examples: It rained all afternoon, so we stayed in.
It rarely rains in the desert.
I hope it does not rain on the day of the picnic.

easy.def: To lift something up.
examples: Raise your hand.
They raised the flag.
He raised the box.

more.def: To lift something up to a higher place.
examples: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
The crew raised the flag.
She raised the window to let in air.

easy.def: To grow plants or care for animals or children.
examples: Farmers raise cows.
They raise chickens.
She raised a puppy.

more.def: To take care of a child or animal as it grows up, or to grow crops.
examples: Farmers in this valley raise sheep.
My grandparents raised four children.
She raised the puppy from the day it was born.

easy.def: To collect money.
examples: We raised money for the shelter.
The class raised fifty dollars.
They raise money for books.

more.def: To collect money for a purpose.
examples: The students raised money for the animal shelter.
Our town raised enough to build a new playground.
We raised a hundred dollars at the bake sale.

easy.def: A big farm for raising cows or horses.
examples: The cowboy lives on a ranch.
The ranch has horses.
We visited a ranch.

more.def: A very large farm where cattle, horses or sheep are raised.
examples: The cowboys on the ranch ride horses every day.
The ranch had thousands of cows.
We spent a week at a ranch in Texas.

easy.def: A line of mountains.
examples: We saw a mountain range.
Snow covers the range.
A long range is far away.

more.def: A group of mountains that are joined together in a long line.
examples: The Rocky Mountains are a long range in North America.
Clouds hung low over the mountain range.
The climbers crossed a high range to reach the valley.

easy.def: To go from one point to another.
examples: Prices range from one to five dollars.
The ages range from six to eight.
The colors range from pale blue to dark.

more.def: To stretch between two limits, from the smallest to the biggest.
examples: Temperatures here range from freezing in winter to hot in summer.
The students range in age from eight to ten.
The books on the shelf range from picture books to long novels.

easy.def: Very fast.
examples: The cheetah is a rapid runner.
The hummingbird's wings are rapid.
He took rapid steps.

more.def: Very quick; happening in a short time.
examples: The river's rapid water carried the raft downstream.
The doctor felt the runner's rapid heartbeat.
The town has seen rapid growth in the last ten years.

easy.def: Not seen or found very much.
examples: It is rare to see snow here.
This is a rare stamp.
A rare bird came to our yard.

more.def: Not common; not often seen, found, or happening.
examples: The zoo has a rare white tiger.
Pandas are rare animals.
It is rare for him to be late.

easy.def: A small animal with a long tail, like a big mouse.
examples: A rat ran across the road.
The rat has a long tail.
Rats can swim.

more.def: A small furry animal with a pointed nose and a long tail, bigger than a mouse.
examples: A rat scurried along the wall.
Some people keep rats as pets.
Rats are good at finding their way through mazes.

easy.def: How fast something goes.
examples: The car moves at a fast rate.
The rate of growth.
The heart's rate.

more.def: How fast something happens or moves.
examples: The car traveled at a rate of sixty miles an hour.
Her heart rate rose when she ran.
Plants grow at different rates.

easy.def: A price for something.
examples: The rate is ten dollars.
The hotel rate.
A low rate.

more.def: The price charged for something, usually by the hour or day.
examples: The hotel's rate is ninety dollars a night.
The rate for the bike was five dollars an hour.
We got a low rate for the cabin.

easy.def: A little bit.
examples: It is rather cold.
She was rather sad.
The test was rather hard.

more.def: To some degree; fairly.
examples: It was rather cold, so we wore our coats.
The box was rather heavy for a small child.
He was rather tired after the long hike.

easy.def: Used to show that you like one thing better.
examples: I would rather play outside.
She would rather have tea.
I would rather read.

more.def: Used to say that you like one choice more than another.
examples: I would rather walk than ride the bus.
She would rather have juice than milk.
Would you rather swim or fish?
